before: Origen went on: Uncover my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law — not as though his eyes were covered, but our eyes are the mind. It belongs to Jesus alone to uncover, so that we may be able to behold the things written and to understand the things said in a hidden way.

The outer man has ears, and the inner man is said to have ears. He who has ears to hear, let him hear. All had the ears of sense, but not all had succeeded in having the inner hearings cleansed. These ears are not in our power; those are in our power. And since it is in our power to have those ears, for this reason the prophet says: Hear, you deaf, and you blind, look up to see. And who is deaf but my servants, and who is blind but those who lord it over them? And the slaves of God were blinded.

That it is in our power to become deaf [lacuna] (let us attend; what is said is about to touch all of us; the inner man must be described so that the blood may be found) — that it is in our power to become deaf according to those hearings, hear the prophet saying: The sinners have been alienated from the womb; they have gone astray from the belly; they have spoken falsehoods. Wrath is theirs according to the likeness of the serpent, as of a deaf asp that stops her ears, which will not listen to the voice of charmers, of a drug being mixed by a wise man (Psalm 119:18) (Matthew 11:15) (Isaiah 42:18–19) (Psalm 58:3–4).

before: Origen went on: And it is possible to be transformed from serpents. For an evil human being is called a serpent and offspring of vipers. If then we want to hear that it is in us to be transformed from serpents, from swine, from dogs, let us learn from the apostle the transformation that is in our power. For he says thus: And we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image.

If you were a barker and the Word formed you and remade you, you have been transformed from a dog into a human being. If you were unclean and the Word reached your soul and you offered yourself to the Word's forming, you have changed from a swine into a human being. If you were beast-like, hearing a word that tames, that domesticates, that changes you into a human being at the will of the Word, you will no longer hear serpent, offspring of vipers. For if it were impossible for these serpents — the serpents according to the soul through vice — to change, the Savior would not have said (or John): Make fruits worthy of repentance, then. Having repented you are no longer a serpent, offspring of vipers.

Since, then, it lies before us to speak about the human being, and to inquire about the soul of the human being whether it is not blood, and the word has required us to arrive at the account of two men in each person, and we have come to a mystical word, we ask you that I may not be charged because of you with throwing the pearls to swine, the holy things to dogs, with casting the divine things to the serpents, with giving a share of the tree of life to the serpent (Matthew 3:7) (2 Corinthians 3:18) (Luke 3:8) (Matthew 3:8) (Matthew 7:6) (Matthew 12:34).

before: Origen went on: We ask you that I may not be charged because of you with throwing the pearls to swine, the holy things to dogs, with casting the divine things to the serpents, with giving a share of the tree of life to the serpent. That I may not be charged, be transformed: put away malice, faction, anger, fights, wrath, griefs, discord, so that there may no longer be schisms among you, but that you may be fitted together in the same mind and the same judgment.

I am in agony both to speak and not to speak. Because of those who are worthy I want to speak, lest I be charged with having deprived of the word those able to hear. Because of those who are not worthy I hesitate to speak, because of what has been said already, lest I ever throw the holy things to dogs and cast the pearls to the swine.

It was the work of Jesus alone to know how to separate, among the hearers, those outside from those inside, so that to those outside he may speak in parables, and to those who have entered his house he may loose the parables. The 'outside' and the entering into the house is mystical. For what is it to me to judge those outside? Everyone who sins is outside. For this reason let it be spoken in parables to those outside, if somehow they may be able, leaving the outside, to become inside. Entering the house is mystical: the genuine disciple of Jesus enters Jesus' house; he enters by thinking the things of the church, by living in the church's way. The inside and the outside is spiritual.

You see how much I say in a preface, preparing the hearers. I hesitate to speak, being about to put it off even while speaking. What do I want to do? To take a word that heals the souls of those who hear.

The human being, then, being created, was first created the one according to the image, of whom matter is not found. For the one according to the image is not from matter either. And God said: Let us make a human being according to our image and according to our likeness, and let them rule, and the rest (Genesis 2:9) (Colossians 3:8) (1 Corinthians 1:10) (Matthew 13:10–13) (Mark 4:11) (1 Corinthians 5:12) (Genesis 1:26) (Genesis 3:22) (Ephesians 4:31).

before: Origen went on: These two men the apostle everywhere sets out, in each person. And it seems to me he has not dared to innovate this account himself, but, having understood more nakedly what the scriptures said more obscurely, has spoken it.

Some think that in the Making of the World, after the creation of the human being, And God took dust from the earth and formed the human being is a repetition. It follows for these people that the 'according to the image' (Genesis 2:7) is the body, and that they grant God to be human-shaped, or that the form of God is according to this figure. But we are not so mad as to say either that God is composite from worse and better, so that the 'according to the image' (Genesis 1:26–27) would be on both, or that the whole [lacuna], God being, the 'according to the image' (Matthew 7:6) has come to be in the worse rather than in the better.

The words are rather fine; we need hearers who have a lean mind. I ask the hearers, then, to watch themselves, lest they ever become the cause of my being charged with throwing the holy things to dogs, to shameless souls. For the barking ones, the dog-like, those stretched toward fornications, toward revilings, do nothing else but yelp, and I must not throw the holy things to such as these. So too I ask the hearers not to become the cause of my being charged with setting pearls of such size — which we try to gather as good merchants — before those who wallow in the uncleannesses of bodies, and who for this reason are called swine.

before: Origen went on: I ask the hearers not to become the cause of my being charged with setting pearls of such size — which we try to gather as good merchants — before those who wallow in the uncleannesses of bodies, and who for this reason are called swine. For I would say that the one who is always rolling in bodily things and wallowing in the mire of life, and not hastening toward the clean life, toward the holy, is in all a swine.

If then, the kingdom of the heavens being likened to a man, a merchant seeking beautiful pearls, I find the beautiful pearls, and having bought them with toils and watchings I throw them to pleasure-loving souls, and to those wallowing in the mires around the bodily things and in the uncleannesses, I too shall have broken the law, because I threw the pearls to the swine. And the swine, receiving the pearls, since they do not see their beauty nor perceive their superiority, trample them — by speaking badly the things said well — and not only do they trample the pearls, but turning they also tear the servants of the pearls.

I beg you, then: be transformed. Do you want to learn that it is in you to be transformed, and to put off the form of the swine, which is according to the unclean soul, and the form of the dog, which is according to the barking and yelping and evil-speaking human being? And it is possible to be transformed from serpents. For an evil human being is called a serpent and offspring of vipers (Matthew 13:45–46) (Matthew 7:6) (2 Corinthians 3:18) (Romans 12:2).
